az_1_lower_highway.blurb: The lowest stretch of the Mount Lemmon road above Tucson sits in Sonoran Desert terrain, about 2,500 feet up, and holds dozens of small crags strung along the roadside. Sport climbing leads by a wide margin, with trad next and a solid bouldering scene alongside a few top-rope lines. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a decent supply of easier routes and a thin tail into the 5.12s. The rock here is more variable in quality than higher on the mountain, so expect uneven stone at some walls. Winter is the draw, when the low elevation keeps conditions comfortable. Bigger clusters include Hairpin Turn Area, Colosseum, Crags Against Humanity and the Molino Basin boulders.

ca_tramway_the.blurb: A bouldering-only zone of scattered granite blocks high in the San Jacinto Mountains, at roughly 8,500 feet. The stone is fine-grained and textured, with edges and crystals, and the problems tend to be steep and featured, rewarding good footwork and powerful, tension-heavy moves; slabs and technical lines are the minority. Grades start below V0 and run into the double digits, but the bulk of problems sit between V0 and V6, so there is plenty for newer boulderers as well as a hard tail. Because of the altitude, summer is the prime season, when the lowlands are too hot, and late spring through fall is the usual window. Shangri-La Valley is the largest sector, followed by Atlantis and Long Valley.

on_golden_horseshoe.blurb: Climbing in the busy region around the western end of Lake Ontario is strung along the Niagara Escarpment. Bouldering makes up the largest share, centred on Niagara Glen, which is almost entirely boulder problems. The roped crags are split fairly evenly between trad and sport, with a few top-rope lines. Mount Nemo is a long, big escarpment crag with sport and trad on its walls, and its north-facing sections suit the early season. Rattlesnake Point mixes top-rope, sport and classic trad, and its south-facing cliff warms quickly in early spring. Boulder grades run from V0 into the V10s, while roped climbs cluster from 5.6 to 5.11, with a few harder lines.

ny_powerlinez.blurb: Set in the southwest corner of a large state park near the New York and New Jersey line, this is a dense collection of short crags and boulders on a wooded plateau. The rock is a hard, gritty granitic gneiss with plenty of friction, and it can be sharp enough to wear skin. Cliffs rarely exceed 50 feet, so the appeal is many technical moves packed close together rather than height. Top-rope lines are the most numerous, followed by bouldering and then single-pitch trad, with only a handful of short bolted routes. Roped grades mostly span 5.6 to 5.10, and boulder problems range from easy up to V10, with a strong spread of V0 to V5. Sectors include East End, Picatinny and Tower Wall area.

nm_taos_area.blurb: Climbing around Taos covers a remote high-desert landscape of northern New Mexico, framed by the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and the Rio Grande rift. The rock changes by sub-area: dark basalt walls in the Rio Grande Gorge, granite slabs and cracks at Tres Piedras and Questa Dome, and metamorphic rock in Comales Canyon. Sport and trad are about equal, backed by a good amount of bouldering. Grades cluster from 5.9 to 5.12, with solid moderates and a few harder lines. Most gorge cliffs face east, so they suit winter mornings and warm-season afternoons, while the higher granite and canyon crags are cooler in midsummer. Tres Piedras, Utopian Vistas and John Dunn Bridge Area are the largest sub-areas.

ca_sheep_pass_area.blurb: A broad, loosely defined district in the middle of Joshua Tree National Park, about 4,200 feet up near the southeast end of Lost Horse Valley. The rock is high-desert monzogranite, and the park as a whole is known for crack, slab and steep face climbing. Trad is the biggest share here, with a lot of bouldering, some top-rope and a smaller amount of sport. Roped grades run mostly from 5.7 to 5.11, with a handful harder, and boulder problems are mostly easy to moderate. Climbing is spread across scattered formations rather than one cliff line, with a handful of long, well-known lines among sparser ground. The biggest sub-areas are Hall of Horrors, Cap Rock, Planet X Area and Saddle Rocks.
